main_issue: When and how Agent D can cook strong-smelling fish curry without disrupting A's calls, B's room and C's laundry

A-B.evidence: A first asked for no strong-smelling cooking (T1). B asked for a heads-up so B could close the door (T8). A later accepted Tue/Thu after 7 (T19); B said thanks to D's notice offer (T10). They never addressed each other directly.

A-C.evidence: A moved from a ban to accepting Tue/Thu after 7 (T5, T19). C said 'that works' to Tue/Thu (T18). Both back the same arrangement.

A-D.evidence: A wanted no strong-smelling food (T1) and D defended the food (T4). A proposed weekends or later evenings (T5); D asked about call times (T6). D proposed Tue/Thu (T17) and A accepted 'Tuesdays and Thursdays after 7' (T19).

B-C.evidence: B (T2) and C (T3) both complained about smell. B accepted a heads-up, C accepted Tue/Thu (T18). They never addressed each other.

B-D.evidence: B complained (T2), then asked D to give notice (T8). D agreed 'I can let you know' (T9) and B thanked D (T10). B never explicitly commented on the Tue/Thu arrangement.

C-D.evidence: C said the heads-up didn't help laundry (T11). D asked about laundry times (T12) and proposed Tue/Thu (T17); C replied 'Okay, that works' (T18).
